Previously both were awaited in one `Promise.all` inside a single Suspense boundary, so the cheap title was held hostage by the 800 ms `getProjectDetails` call. - `` renders outside any Suspense boundary → it lands in the prerendered shell. - `<Details>` sits behind its own Suspense boundary and starts with `await connection()`. - `generateStaticParams` prerenders a per-slug shell, which is what lets the *resolved* title (not just the slug) be in the shell. **`lib/data.ts`** — added `getProjectSlugs()` (also `'use cache'`) to feed `generateStaticParams`. The `connection()` call is the load-bearing part for your second requirement. Without it the route builds as fully static (`○`), because `getProjectDetails` is `'use cache'` and therefore prerenderable — so the default prefetch pulled the whole page. I confirmed that against the running server: the prefetch payload contained `Commerce storefront` and the activity list. `connection()` pushes that subtree to request time only; the `'use cache'` on `getProjectDetails` still applies, so it's a cache read on navigation, not a refetch. Measured on `next start`, `/projects/acme`: | request | payload | |---|---| | prefetch (`Next-Router-Prefetch: 1`) | 1294 b — `Acme Storefront` + `Loading details` fallback | | navigation (full RSC) | 1941 b — adds description + activity | Route table went from `○ /projects/acme` (fully static, everything prefetched) to `◐ /projects/acme`. Per-slug titles check out: `orbit` prefetches `Orbit Analytics`, and an unlisted slug like `/projects/unknown` gets a runtime shell with `Unknown project`. Initial HTML TTFB is 5 ms with `<h1>Acme Storefront</h1>` already in it. I left the dashboard's `<Link>` alone — the default `prefetch` (`"auto"`) fetches the static shell only, which is exactly the behavior you want. Setting `prefetch={true}` would undo this and pull the dynamic details too. Two incidental notes: `next build` rewrote `tsconfig.json` itself (`jsx: react-jsx` plus type includes), and the build produced untracked `.next/` and `next-env.d.ts` — your `.gitignore` only lists `node_modules/` and `__agent_eval__/`, so you may want to add those.

(timeout 120 npx next start -p 3111 > /tmp/next.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 6; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3111/

cd /workspace
echo "--- TREE prefetch"; curl -s "http://localhost:3111/projects/acme" -H 'RSC: 1' -H 'Next-Router-Prefetch: 1' -H 'next-router-segment-prefetch: /_tree' | tr -d '\0' | grep -o "Acme Storefront\|Commerce storefront" | sort -u
echo "--- PAGE segment prefetch"; curl -s "http://localhost:3111/projects/acme" -H 'RSC: 1' -H 'Next-Router-Prefetch: 1' -H 'next-router-segment-prefetch: /projects/$d$slug/__PAGE__' | tr -d '\0' | grep -o "Acme Storefront\|Commerce storefront" | sort -u
echo "--- full prefetch (auto, no segment header)"; curl -s "http://localhost:3111/projects/acme" -H 'RSC: 1' -H 'Next-Router-Prefetch: 1' | tr -d '\0' | grep -o "Acme Storefront\|Commerce storefront" | sort -u

cd /workspace
for seg in '/_tree' '/projects/$d$slug/__PAGE__'; do echo "=== $seg"; curl -s --compressed "http://localhost:3111/projects/acme" -H 'RSC: 1' -H 'Next-Router-Prefetch: 1' -H "next-router-segment-prefetch: $seg" -D /tmp/h.txt -o /tmp/body.bin; grep -i "^x-nextjs\|^content-\|^HTTP" /tmp/h.txt; wc -c /tmp/body.bin; strings /tmp/body.bin | grep -i "acme\|storefront\|Loading\|h1" | head -5; done

cd /workspace

probe TREE '/_tree'
probe PAGESEG '/projects/$d$slug/__PAGE__'
